answer: Each agent claims one distinct spring in an oasis pool and locks a 70-credit bond. The first entry costs 30 credits; the k-th pays 30+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6024 and 1000 fake springs cost 3,027,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked, with no spring or bond shared. Each epoch the holder signs a pulse proving the same key holds it; the keeper checks each signature, and a copied pulse triggers a ripple audit, then burns the bond. A rented-spring ring fails because one rented spring yields only one valid pulse per epoch, so each extra identity needs its own spring. An honest agent pays 30 once.
